title: File:Leucanthemum vulgare habit4 (14609961126).jpg
author: Harry Rose from South West Rocks, Australia
description: Introduced, cool-season, perennial, erect herb, typically 30-60 cm tall and with shallow rhizomes and roots. Stem leaves are alternate, stem clasping and toothed or pinnately lobed. Flowerheads of 1-3 heads. Heads are 3-6 cm diameter, with white ligulate ray flowers and yellow tubular disc flowers. Flowers mostly spring and summer. A garden escape that is now a weed, especially in disturbed or low ground cover situations, including native grasslands, roadsides and overgrazed pastures. Mainly grows in temperate regions where annual rainfall exceeds 750 mm; prefers low pH, low nutrient and heavy damp soils. Low quality and densely-growing, it can exclude other pasture species and reduce the carry capacity. Eaten by horses, sheep and goats, but avoided by cattle; will taint milk if grazed. Especially spreads where cattle graze, becoming more of a problem as grazing pressure increases. Effective controls include intensive cultivation, good grazing management, mob stocking of cattle, fertilisers (especially nitrogen) and herbicides.

title: File:Common dandelion (Taraxacum officinale) - geograph.org.uk - 819620.jpg
author: Kate Jewell
description: Common dandelion (Taraxacum officinale) Along side the disused Grantham Canal towpath there were hundreds of dandelion clocks. The common name derives from the French 'dent de lion', meaning 'lion's tooth', which refers to the deeply toothed, deep green leaves. The bright yellow flower heads are borne on hollow stalks, and the downy seed heads are familiar to children as dandelion clocks, which are used to 'tell the time' by the number of blows taken to remove the seeds. Vernacular names for the dandelion include 'wet-the-bed' and 'pissy-beds', which refer to the belief that just touching part of a dandelion can cause bed-wetting.

title: File:Dandelion (Taraxacum officinale) in Shimla.jpg
author: Sapna Sony
description: Dandelion seed head (Taraxacum officinale) photographed in Sarog village, Shimla district, Himachal Pradesh, India. The image shows the plant in its seed stage after the yellow flower has bloomed. The round white fluffy structure is made up of many tiny seeds, each attached to a soft, parachute-like part that helps them spread through the wind. This stage is often called the “dandelion clock.” Dandelions are perennial plants commonly found in lawns, fields, grasslands, and along roadsides. They are widely distributed and grow easily in many different environments.

title: File:Dandelion bud (Taraxacum officinale) in Shimla.jpg
author: Sapna Sony
description: Dandelion bud of Taraxacum officinale photographed in Sarog village, Shimla district, Himachal Pradesh, India. The image shows the plant in a closed bud stage before the flower fully opens or transitions into seed formation. The green bracts surrounding the flower head protect the developing florets. Dandelions commonly grow in open grassy habitats and are widely distributed across temperate regions.

title: File:Flowering Dandelion (Taraxacum officinale) in Shimla.jpg
author: Sapna Sony
description: Flowering dandelion (Taraxacum officinale) photographed in Sarog village, Shimla district, Himachal Pradesh, India. The image shows the plant in its blooming stage with a bright yellow composite flower head made up of many small florets. title: File:Hibiscus rosa -sinensis.jpg
author: Gabriel De Aza
description: This captivating image captures the vibrant beauty of a Hibiscus rosa-sinensis flower in its full splendor. With delicate petals of an intense red hue and a prominent pistil, the flower unfolds with elegance, highlighting its natural grace. The dark green leaves, richly textured, serve as a backdrop, enhancing the intensity of the floral color. The careful composition allows one to appreciate the intricate details of the flower, from the veins on the petals to the subtle nuances of color. The soft light accentuates the plant's features, creating a charming contrast between the vibrant tones and the serene background. This photograph, taken with dedication and a passion for flora, seeks to illustrate the exquisite beauty of Hibiscus rosa-sinensis, a species that captivates with its lush presence and ornamental symbolism.

title: File:Hibiscus Flower (Hibiscus rosa-sinensis).jpg
author: Jeremyida002
description: The hibiscus flower is a vibrant and versatile flowering plant known for its large, trumpet-shaped blossoms that come in various colors such as red, pink, yellow, and white. Belonging to the mallow family, Hibiscus has over 200 species and is native to warm climates. It is widely cultivated for ornamental purposes in gardens and landscapes. Additionally, certain species like Hibiscus sabdariffa have culinary and medicinal uses, with the plant's calyces being used to make herbal teas and infusions that are believed to have various health benefits. Hibiscus is celebrated for its aesthetic appeal and cultural significance in different parts of the world.

title: File:Common sunflower (Helianthus annuus).jpg
author: Dandy1022
description: Common sunflower, Yokohama City , Japan Helianthus annuus [1] Q171497 [2] , the Common sunflower is a large annual forb of the genus Helianthus grown as a crop for its edible oil and edible fruits. The plant was first domesticated in the Americas . Genus: : Helianthus ( Sunflowers ) Family: Asteraceae Daisy, Compositae, Aster, Composite, Sunflower Interesting Facts Most people think that the sunflower name is based on the direction of sunrise and sunset. However, this is not the case. Blooming sunflowers face east and do not rotate in the direction of the sun. Nevertheless, the misconception that it faces the sun is deeply embedded in people's minds. Therefore, it is commonly called a sunflower. Wild versions of the plant branch out to many flower heads, but domesticated plants typically only have one. In culture: These flowers were worshipped by the ancient Incas , and today they represent an eco-friendly movements. Vincent Van Gogh made a famous series of paintings about common sunflowers .
